Stage 3 · Grammar

Grammar

I'd like a coffee · some / any
FormUseExample
a / anone countablea coffee, an apple
some+ plural / uncountablesome chips, some water
any– and ?We don't have any juice.
Do you have any juice?
I'd likepolite orderI'd like a coffee, please.
  • a/an = one thing you can count: a sandwich, an apple. Plural or uncountable → some: some chips, some water.
  • some in + sentences; any in – and ?: I have some milk. I don't have any tea. Do you have any juice?
  • Order politely: I'd like (= I would like) a coffee, please. Can I have some water?
  • Ask what things are: What's a croque monsieur? — It's a hot sandwich.

→ Shopping & prices (How much is it?) come next.

🔧 Build it yourself
  • 🔧 Build it yourself
  • Build it: + some → I'd like SOME chips. – and ? → any: Do you have ANY juice?
  • ⚠ I'd like = я бы хотел (polite order). I like = мне нравится. Don't mix them in a café!

Stage 6 · Speaking

Your turn

Write a short café order: I'd like … / Can I have some … .

When you finish, open the model answer and check yourself.

Model answer

I'd like a coffee and a croissant, please. Can I have some water too? No chips, thank you.

Check yourself:

  • Did you use I'd like / Can I have…?
  • Did you choose a / some correctly (a coffee, some water)?
  • Did you add please / thank you?
Talk to Sam. Answer with the words from this lesson.

Read each message. Tap 🔊 to hear Sam.

Sam

Hi! Welcome to my café. ☕

Sam

Can I help you? 😊

Sam

Sure! ☕

Sam

Anything to eat? 🥪

Sam

Of course! 🍟

Sam

Listen: “Can I have a water?” 🤔

Why

water is uncountable → some water (not 'a water'). For one countable thing: a coffee, a sandwich.

Sam

Yes! “Can I have some water?” Great catch. 🌟

Feedback

Well done: you ordered with I'd like and some/any. Next time, say it out loud too.
